profile.headline: SDE II at Amazon Robotics
profile.summary:
I'm an electronics and software expert (FPGAs, Python, C++), who seeks difficult and complex projects. I specifically like developing innovative solutions for cutting edge problems of all types. I'm well practiced at defining what needs to be done from first principles, being aware of the state-of-the-art in technological tools available, developing a framework and architecture, digging deep into the technical details to overcome any roadblock, and executing on the delivery.

I currently work at Amazon Robotics!

I take a particular interest in understanding the project from a top-level view, and have continued to explore leadership, entrepreneurship, project management and mentoring. I think communication is critical in the workplace, and I have developed an intuition for explaining complicated concepts and details to non-technical experts. 

I worked at BNL as an electronics engineer, which is a great match for my skills. I have developed FPGA and software readout systems, Printed Circuit Board design, and overall electronics architecture for a variety of projects. I've worked in big scientific collaborations such as DUNE, nEXO, and DarkSide, where the electronics need to be submerged in cryogenic liquids, necessitating in-depth testing and characterization of every component and cable. I've worked on a variety of smaller research projects internally and with private companies in areas such as quantum computing and nanomaterials. My final project was LuSEE, a lunar lander project going to the moon in a few years, on its FPGA architecture and Digital Signal Processing!

I've always been a tinkerer after work hours. One of my projects that grew into a patent and manufactured consumer electronics product was the Kegr, an automated electronic keg tap, which links to a smartphone app for precision control. I truly enjoyed designing the product, the embedded software coding, developing the apps, securing funding and doing all the work necessary to put it out there!

I'll always have a zest for learning new things, challenging myself, and playing music. Check me out on the accordion and guitar!

positions.title: Software Developer Engineer II - R&D Engineering
Electronic Engineer II
positions.description:
- Utilized System on Chip FPGAs (Xilinx Zynq Ultrascale+, MicroChip PolarFire) to implement soft core Linux and microcontroller functionality

- LuSEE (a lunar lander project) required learning the Microchip FPGA family due to radiation-hardness requirements.

- Developed FPGA DSP blocks using low level VHDL coding and high-level synthesis tools.

- Extensive experience with build automation, TCL scripting, simulation, testing and verification

- Automated FPGA debugging tools for productivity – ILAs, Signaltap, Synopsis Identify, ModelSim

- Designed, prototyped, and characterized custom FPGA PCBs, connector/cabling schemes, eye diagrams, BERTs

- Designed back-end software architectures to read, analyze and store incoming high-speed experimental data, implementing custom network packet structures, ZeroMQ, ring buffers, compression, etc…

- Extensive experience with Python for automating general computing tasks, creating command line interfaces, and analyzing data with NumPy, Matplotlib, SciPy, etc…

- Use Manjaro Linux as primary operating system, general working knowledge of the Linux operating system

- Wrote multiple GUI interfaces in PyQT and Tkinter for use by non-technical experts

- Use Git for revision control of large software/FPGA projects across multiple organizations, as well as Docker

positions.title: Electronics Engineer I
positions.description:
- Worked in multiple international scientific collaborations (DUNE, SBND, nEXO, DarkSide) designing, prototyping, testing and delivering state of the art cryogenic electronic systems. Collaborated with scientific personnel across research institutions and universities, conducting trade studies, writing papers.

- Programmed FPGAs (VHDL) to interface with ASIC readout boards and handle power distribution, SPI communication, high speed ADC readout, Gigabit Ethernet output with custom UDP packets, JESD204B.

- Awarded a $1M Laboratory Directed Research and Development (LDRD) focused on researching, fabricating, and testing solutions for high-speed electronic communication with specific requirements as demanded by experiments (low radioactive background, no outgassing, certain CTE, no FR-4).

- Developed automated characterization sequences for screening of ASIC productions runs using custom PCBs with diagnostic abilities - multiplexers, DACs, arbitrary waveform generators.  

- Test sequences consisted of Python scripts communicating with the FPGA to read out ASICS in various test configurations

- Wrote a GUI front end (Tkinter library) for graduate students, saved data using Sumatra (Python).

- Performed a variety of data analysis, making extensive use of visual plotting with the Matplotlib library.

- Designed and implemented automated test setups and triggering schemes between various instruments (digital multimeters, oscilloscopes, power supplies) with PyVISA or Labview as a base framework.

- Wrote comprehensive technical documentation including complex figures (timing diagrams, schematics) in LaTeX.

- Designed PCBs for internally developed ASICs (analog preamplifiers, ADCs).

- Designed and tested analog circuits and components for performance at cryogenic temperatures.

- Became a mentor for graduate students, personally mentored a high school student over a year.

positions.title: Electrical Engineering Intern
positions.description:
- Wrote a thesis on silicon photomultiplier array behavior at cryogenic temperatures

- Regularly used instruments such as oscilloscopes, semiconductor device analyzers, DMMs

- Designed test setups and measured the behavior of inductors and dielectrics at cryogenic temperatures

- Coded custom MATLAB scripts for data processing

- Designed multiple PCB schematics and assisted in PCB layout, assembly, and modification

- Designed 3D printed fixtures and elements of test setups as needed

positions.title: CEO/Founder
positions.description:
https://thekegr.com/

- Awarded US Patent US10618794B2 for an electronic keg tap with Bluetooth connectivity.

- Programmed embedded Bluetooth Low Energy microcontroller (nRF52) for desired functionality

- Programmed Android and iOS connectivity apps

- Designed mechanical architecture, underwent sourcing, testing, validation to bring product to market.

- Developed automated testing scheme for QA/QC in Python.

- Presented to investors, fundraised.

- Developed a business and advertising plan and executed on it.

positions.title: Manufacturing Engineer
positions.description: I analyzed and improved existing manufacturing processes for electromechanical relays, as well as researched and implemented new ones.  From laser welding machines to proprietary electrical testing equipment to industrial ovens with multiple control zones, I have experience integrating new technologies into an existing production line with minimal downtime.  The breadth of my responsibilities were widened, encompassing CNC programming, failure analysis, and technical training.

positions.title: Staff Engineer
positions.description: I participated in a variety of environmental engineering projects, from long term cleanups, to spill responses, to work requiring adherence to regulations.  I used electronic instrumentation to measure groundwater contamination and report on it to the Department of Environmental Protection.

positions.title: Work Study
positions.description: Worked with professors and department secretaries to make copies, scans, faxes, and was responsible for administrative duties such as the availability of office supplies.

positions.title: Engineering Co-Op/Intern
positions.description:
As a co-op, I became familiar with the failure analysis side of semiconductor manufacturing.  While working in the process lab of the failure analysis department, I performed destructive and non-destructive analysis of electronic components and semiconductors that had failed tests on the manufacturing line or that had been returned by customers.

I also worked with manufacturing engineers to perform physical tests on electronic modules to collect data on failure methods due to factors such as thermal or force loads.  I utilized a variety of methods, such as an Instron device, Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM), Differential Scanning Calorimeter, and Thermomechanical and Thermogravitational Analyzers.

I gained experience in fields relating to manufacturing and electrical engineering through constant exposure to electrical schematics, various methods of analysis, such as chemical decaps, and weekly meetings with lead engineers analyzing current trends and data.

positions.title: Engineering Intern
positions.description: As an intern, I conducted a variety of field analyses, collecting data such as samples and measurements, and assisted in creating engineering reports and AutoCAD drawings.
